target.title: fix(media-understanding): suppress default English audio prompt for non-English transcription
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Groq Whisper (and OpenAI-compatible STT providers) treat the audio transcription `prompt` field as a **biasing hint**, not an instruction. OpenClaw always sent the default English prompt `Transcribe the audio.` even when a non-English `language` hint was configured, which biased short non-English voice notes toward English translation despite the explicit language hint.

Reported in #98970: a short Russian Telegram voice note with `language=ru` returned the English translation `"Do it."` instead of the Russian transcript `делаете`. Direct Groq comparison on the same audio confirmed the cause:

```
language=ru, no prompt      -> делаете      (correct Russian transcript)
language=ru, English prompt -> Do it.       (English translation — OpenClaw's behavior)
language=ru, Russian prompt -> Делайте.
```

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolvePrompt` (`src/media-understanding/resolve.ts`) applied the same default prompt logic to every capability. For audio, that meant the English `Transcribe the audio.` default was injected whenever no explicit `prompt` was configured — independent of the configured `language`. Because Whisper's `prompt` biases decoding, the English default steered non-English clips toward English.

The fix makes `resolvePrompt` **language-aware for audio**:
- An explicit `prompt` always wins (unchanged behavior for users who set one).
- When no explicit prompt is set **and** a non-English language is configured, the default English prompt is **suppressed** (resolved to `""`), so the provider honors the `language` hint alone.
- English hints (`en`, `en-US`, `english`, …) and the no-language case keep the existing default prompt — no behavior change for English transcription.

English detection covers BCP-47 tags and bare words (`en`, `eng`, `english`, `en-*`, `en_*`); anything else is treated as non-English.

`resolveEntryRunOptions` threads the resolved `language` (entry → capability config → `tools.media.<capability>.language`) into `resolvePrompt` so the same precedence used to build the request's `language` field governs prompt suppression.

## User Impact

- Non-English voice notes (e.g. Russian, Chinese) are transcribed **in the requested language** instead of being silently translated to English when no custom audio prompt is set.
- Users who set a custom `tools.media.audio.prompt` see no change — explicit prompts still pass through verbatim.
- English transcription is unchanged.

## Evidence

Production-function probe calling the patched `resolvePrompt` from source (`node --import tsx`):

```text
node --import tsx --no-warnings -e "
import { resolvePrompt } from './src/media-understanding/resolve.js';
const cases = [
  { cap: 'audio', label: 'no prompt, no language (default English)' },
  { cap: 'audio', lang: 'ru', label: 'no prompt, language=ru' },
  { cap: 'audio', lang: 'zh-CN', label: 'no prompt, language=zh-CN' },
  { cap: 'audio', lang: 'en', label: 'no prompt, language=en' },
  { cap: 'audio', lang: 'en-US', label: 'no prompt, language=en-US' },
  { cap: 'audio', prompt: 'Transcribe verbatim.', lang: 'ru', label: 'explicit prompt + ru' },
];
for (const c of cases) {
  const p = resolvePrompt(c.cap, c.prompt, undefined, c.lang);
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ label: c.label, language: c.lang ?? null, resolved: p }));
}
"
```

Output:

```text
{"label":"no prompt, no language (default English)","language":null,"resolved":"Transcribe the audio."}
{"label":"no prompt, language=ru","language":"ru","resolved":""}
{"label":"no prompt, language=zh-CN","language":"zh-CN","resolved":""}
{"label":"no prompt, language=en","language":"en","resolved":"Transcribe the audio."}
{"label":"no prompt, language=en-US","language":"en-US","resolved":"Transcribe the audio."}
{"label":"explicit prompt + ru","language":"ru","resolved":"Transcribe verbatim."}
```

The `""` result means `buildAudioTranscriptionFormData` (`src/media-understanding/shared.ts`) skips the `prompt` multipart field (it drops empty/whitespace values), so the provider receives `language=ru` with no `prompt` — matching the direct-Groq "stays Russian" case from the issue.

Regression tests (all passing):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media-understanding/resolve.test.ts src/media-understanding/runner.auto-audio.test.ts
```

- `resolve.test.ts`: 12/12 passed — new `resolvePrompt` block covers default, explicit-prompt-wins, non-English suppression (`ru`, `zh-CN`), English retention (`en`, `en-US`), and non-audio length guidance.
- `runner.auto-audio.test.ts`: 11/11 passed — new cases assert the full runner sends `prompt=""` with `language="ru"`, and `"Transcribe the audio."` with no language, proving the fix flows through `resolveEntryRunOptions` into the provider request.

Adjacent suite confirmed unaffected (no regression in the shared OpenAI-compatible audio adapter):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media-understanding/openai-compatible-audio.test.ts   # 7/7 passed
```

## Scope

- `src/media-understanding/resolve.ts` — `resolvePrompt` gains an optional `language` arg and audio-specific language-aware branching; new local `isNonEnglishLanguage` helper.
- `src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts` — `resolveEntryRunOptions` resolves `language` (same precedence as the request `language` field) and passes it to `resolvePrompt`.
- Tests added in `resolve.test.ts` and `runner.auto-audio.test.ts`.

No config/default surface is added or removed — this reuses the existing `tools.media.audio.language` (and per-entry/per-capability `language`) fields already consumed to build the request. Non-audio capabilities are untouched.

## Not tested

- Live Groq/OpenAI Whisper request against a real non-English voice note (no provider credentials in this environment). The unit + runner tests assert the request payload shape (`prompt=""`, `language="ru"`) that reproduces the issue's "no prompt stays Russian" direct-Groq result.
- Local CLI audio entries (e.g. `whisper-cli`): they receive `Prompt` via template substitution and are unaffected by this change since they don't use `resolvePrompt`'s audio branch for the request `prompt` field — verified the CLI path still uses `requestOverrides.prompt ?? prompt` for its `{{Prompt}}` template.

Closes #98970
